Smooth k-Conservative Vector Fields We now explicitly construct the space of smooth, k-conservative vector fields. Given V ∈ C ∞ (Rn ), let J(V ) : Rn → Rn×n denote its Jacobian, which we can view as an n × n matrix over C ∞ (Rn , R). If V ∈ C ∞ (Rn ), then by the Poincaré lemma (Warner, 1983, Section 4.18), V is k-conservative if and only if J(V k ) is symmetric.
